title: Why Feeling Great Is the Danger When the Oxygen Masks Drop
topic: Why a cabin pressure loss gives you only seconds of useful consciousness
mechanism: A jet pumps its cabin up to an eight-thousand-foot pressure; when it leaks, hypoxia arrives as euphoria instead of fear, so at thirty-five thousand feet you get thirty to sixty seconds to pull the mask that fires a chemical oxygen generator while the pilots dive to ten thousand feet.

beats.hook: When the oxygen masks drop, the most dangerous thing on the plane is how good you feel: Barry giggles under the swinging masks.
beats.but: Outside, the air is so thin it cannot keep a brain running, so the jet squeezes the cabin to an eight-thousand-foot pressure.
beats.then: A door seal cracks, the air screams out, the cabin fogs, the cabin-altitude needle climbs and the masks drop before fifteen thousand.
beats.conflict: Grandma Rose helps everyone else first while Barry pokes the flat bag and laughs; nobody screams.
beats.pivot: You see, a brain starving for oxygen does not feel fear, it feels a warm, happy buzz, and at this height that buzz gives you thirty to sixty seconds.
beats.so: So the attendant shouts to pull the mask: the yank fires a chemical oxygen generator, the pilots mask up and dive to ten thousand feet, and the plane wakes up.
beats.closing: Up there, feeling great is the warning. Mask first, then help.
